properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked): reflow2 is absent from Copilot's tool list because the organisation's Copilot policy blocks third-party MCP servers. Nothing in reflow2 causes it. MCP is reflow2's only way to register as an agent tool, and the two other ways (a registry allowlist, a VS Code Language Model Tools extension) were settled on 2026-10-01 as unavailable or not pursued. What reflow2 does own is the hand-written instructions file, and that is limitation 11, already planned
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triage agent B. Item L1 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02: "Not a tool in Copilot's tool list. Reachable only because an instructions file says so."

① OBSERVED: reflow2's tools are not in Copilot's tool list, and the agent uses them only because a user-scope instructions file teaches it `--call`.

② PRECEDENT: dec:idea-where-an-org-blocks-third-party-mcp-ask-for-an-allowlist-before-building-around-it (settled 2026-10-01): the allowlist was asked for and refused ("very hard to change"), and an extension is not pursued. rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground makes MCP reflow2's one assumption about an agent.

③ CANDIDATES IN REFLOW2, each checked:
(a) init registers reflow2 for VS Code wrongly. NO. reflow2_init.py's vscode entry writes .vscode/mcp.json `servers`, which is the right file for VS Code. The policy, not the file, keeps it out.
(b) reflow2 offers a non-MCP registration and it failed. NO. None exists.
(c) the instructions file is reflow2's. PARTLY: it is one person's hand-written file. init and update neither install nor refresh it. That is limitation 11, planned in req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current.

CONCLUSION: the cause is the organisation's policy, plainly. reflow2's choice of MCP as its only agent interface is what makes the block total, and that choice is settled intent, not a defect. Nothing measured contradicts the report. NOT MEASURED HERE: the work machine's policy itself, which was relayed by Anthony.

One related fact from the VS Code documentation, for the planned fix: VS Code reads project Agent Skills from .github/skills and .claude/skills, and lists them beside the agent's tools as "/" commands. Skill stubs are the nearest thing to native presence the policy may allow (fact:root-cause-vs-code-reads-project-skills-and-slash-prompts-and-init-installs-neither-for-it-2026-10-02).
